summary: Add first-class alert tags so operators can assign, remove, and filter alerts by tag.

acceptance_criteria.text: Add a new Tag concept with a many-to-many relationship to Alert persisted via EF Core migration.
POST /api/alerts/{id}/tags adds one or more tags with case-insensitive dedupe, max 10 tags per alert, and each tag length 1 to 30.
DELETE /api/alerts/{id}/tags/{tag} removes a tag assignment and returns 404 when the alert or assignment does not exist.
GET /api/alerts supports an optional tag filter that composes with existing filters.
AlertResponse includes tags for each returned alert.

implementation_steps: 1. Add Tag and AlertTag entities in AlertService.Models/Tag.cs and AlertService.Models/AlertTag.cs and extend AlertService.Models/Alert.cs navigation.
2. Extend contracts in AlertService.DTO/Requests/AlertQueryRequest.cs and AlertService.DTO/Responses/AlertResponse.cs for tag input and output.
3. Extend data abstraction in AlertService.Data/Interfaces/IAlertRepository.cs with tag operations and tag-aware list filtering.

4. Add EF mappings in AlertService.Data.SQL/Configurations/TagConfiguration.cs and AlertService.Data.SQL/Configurations/AlertTagConfiguration.cs and register sets in AlertService.Data.SQL/AlertDbContext.cs.
5. Implement tag query and assignment persistence in AlertService.Data.SQL/Repositories/AlertRepository.cs.
6. Update mapping in AlertService.API/Mappings/AlertMappingExtensions.cs to project tags in responses.
7. Add service signatures in AlertService.API/Services/IAlertService.cs and business logic in AlertService.API/Services/AlertManagementService.cs.
8. Add tag endpoints in AlertService.API/Controllers/AlertsController.cs with expected status codes.

9. Add EF migration artifacts in AlertService.Data.SQL/Migrations/<timestamp>_AddAlertTags.cs, AlertService.Data.SQL/Migrations/<timestamp>_AddAlertTags.Designer.cs, and AlertService.Data.SQL/Migrations/AlertDbContextModelSnapshot.cs.

planned_tests.test: Repository persists alerts with tags and loads joined tags through normal query paths.
Migration model enforces unique normalized tag value and composite join key constraints.
Controller and service add multiple tags to an existing alert and return updated tag list.
Adding tags to a missing alert returns not found behavior from service and controller.
Service dedupes case-insensitive duplicates and rejects invalid length or max-count overflow.
Deleting an existing tag assignment removes the relation and reports success.
Deleting a tag from a missing alert or missing assignment returns not found behavior.
Repository GetAll applies tag filter together with isActive, severity, date, and search filters.
Tag filter matching is case-insensitive and yields empty results when no matching tag exists.
AlertResponse mapping includes all assigned tags for list and detail responses.

contract_changes.api: Add POST /api/alerts/{id}/tags and DELETE /api/alerts/{id}/tags/{tag}, add optional tag query filter, and include tags in AlertResponse.
contract_changes.database: Add Tags and AlertTags tables with indexes, foreign keys, and relationship snapshot updates.

boundaries.primary_slice: Alert CRUD API, service orchestration, and SQL repository with EF Core model updates.
out_of_scope: Regenerating database/02_AlertServiceDb_Migrations.sql is deferred to migration script generation workflow.
Non-tag API behavior and summary endpoint semantics remain unchanged.

assumptions: Tag endpoints return the updated AlertResponse payload to keep behavior aligned with existing update-style endpoints.
risks: Medium: tag normalization and dedupe rules can drift between API and database unless one canonical strategy is used; rollback = revert tag model and migration changes together.
scope_override_reason: This story spans API contracts, business rules, EF model, migration artifacts, and mapping so the source-file cap is intentionally exceeded.
constraints: Q1: tag casing strategy for dedupe and output -> force lowercase
Q2: behavior when adding tags exceeds max 10 -> reject with 400
